subrules.rule: Each Transcend card has a striated text box containing two transcend level bars. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the left side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.

A transcend ability bar is a keyword ability that represents an activated ability. A transcend ability bar includes the activation cost of its activated ability and a subtype. Any abilities printed within the same text box section as the transcend ability bar are part of its activated ability.

subrules.name: 745.2a
subrules.rule: “[Cost]: [Subtype] — [Effect]” printed on a Transcend card means “[Cost]: This permanent becomes a [Subtype] in addition to its other types. Put a +1/+1 counter on it. [Effect]. Activate this ability only once, only as a sorcery, and only if each of its previous transcend abilities have been activated.”

subrules.name: 745.2b
subrules.rule: The phrase “previous transcend abilities” refers to each ability printed on the Transcend card above the ability being activated. It is possible for an object to gain multiple groups of transcend abilities, these abilities from other cards are not counted as previous transcend abilities, even if they happen to come from cards with the same name.

Any ability printed on a Transcend card that isn’t preceded by a transcend ability bar is treated normally. In particular, the Transcend card has the ability printed in its top text box section at all times. That ability may affect the game if it’s a static ability, it may trigger if it’s a triggered ability, and it can be activated if it’s an activated ability.

subrules.rule: Each Diverge cards has a striated text box containing two divergent paths. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the left side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.

A divergent ability is a keyword ability that represents an activated ability. A divergent path includes the activation cost of its activated ability and a subtype. Any abilities printed within the same text box section as the divergent path are part of its activated ability.

subrules.name: 750.2a
subrules.rule: "[Cost]: [Subtype] — [Effect]" printed on a Diverge card means "[Cost]: This permanent becomes a [Subtype] in addition to its other types. Put a +1/+1 counter on it. [Effect]. Activate this ability only as a sorcery, and only if none of its divergent paths have been activated."

subrules.name: 750.2b
subrules.rule: One card (Quarry of the Ivory Mask) allows players to activate diverge abilities any time they could cast an instant. This effect allows players to ignore the timing restriction associated with divergent paths. Players will still be unable to activate an object's divergent paths in response to its first activation, even if that ability hasn't resolved yet.

subrules.name: 750.2c
subrules.rule: It is possible for an object to gain multiple pairs of divergent paths. If the permanent has activated any divergent paths, including any it may no longer have, it will still be unable to activate paths from these alternate groups.

Any ability printed on a Diverge card that isn't preceded by a divergent path is treated normally. In particular, the Diverge card has the abilities printed in its top text box sections at all times. That ability may affect the game if it’s a static ability, it may trigger if it’s a triggered ability, and it can be activated if it’s an activated ability.
